what_happened: GHR 1994 Chapter 10 section 10.2 -- the exact ZTime separation section this task must formalize, Lemmas 10.2.1-10.2.8 and Theorem 10.2.9 -- is present IN FULL in the corpus at /home/benjamin/Projects/Literature/sources/gabbay_1994/ch1001_chapter-10-expressive-completeness-of-si.md, despite the literature briefing's chapter-10 entries advertising only sections 10.3.1 and 10.3.2. Full step map extractable without reading the PDF.

GHR94 Lemma 10.2.3's printed formula for Case 5 is refuted over integer time by an explicit counterexample (a(0), A(1), B identically false, q(1)=q(2); LHS true at t=3, RHS false since both printed disjuncts carry the conjunct [A or (B and U(A,B))] evaluated at t). Verified against the ch10 PDF text, not only the markdown chunk -- the PDF layout carries the same conjunct on the second disjunct, which also contradicts GHR's own gloss that the second disjunct covers the case where A is true in the PAST. A gloss-consistent reconstruction (dropping that conjunct from disjunct 2) survives the counterexample on that model. Implementation must RECONSTRUCT and independently verify Cases 5-8, not transcribe them.

Two major pre-existing assets found. (1) plusValidZTime_iff_plusValidInt (FormalSystem/PlusLanguage/PlusIntTransfer.lean, live and compiled) collapses the ZTime carrier quantifier to the single carrier Z, so the whole elimination layer can be proved over concrete integers rather than over an abstract successor-Archimedean ordered group. (2) An archived GHR 10.2 transcription of about 10,300 lines exists at Boneyard/Kamp/KampWeakCanonical/Separation/ (Eliminations.lean cases 1-4 worked, Hierarchy/ carrying junction_depth, count_U_subformulas, abstract_untl, subst roundtrip and an all_formulas_separable skeleton) -- unchecked (#exit, never compiled) but a usable architectural blueprint.

All seven pinned Lean Challenge Statements were compile-verified at plan time: lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --dry-run --compile assembled the Challenge module and reported 'compile: OK' against the repo toolchain, so every contract signature is known to type-check against the existing vocabulary before implementation starts.

The research report's illustrative USForm sketch indexes leaves by Fin n; the plan replaces it with an unparameterized USForm indexed by the natural numbers (Decision D-a), because GHR's fresh-atom abstraction/resubstitution steps would otherwise incur a Fin-cast obligation at every one of Lemmas 10.2.5-10.2.8. Recorded as a deliberate deviation from the report's sketch, not a correction of it.

The pre-commit typst-sync-check.sh --counts-only gate fires on every module-adding commit because typst/generated/status.typ pins FormalSystem file/line counts. Plan Phase 14 owns that file, but the gate forces the regeneration at each module-adding phase commit instead. Resolution: run scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix and stage typst/generated/status.typ in every module-adding phase commit; Phase 14 then only has to confirm, not re-derive.

Phase 5 DECISION GATE measured 1 of 4, not 4 of 4. A Case 5 candidate was derived from the semantics (split on the pure-future U(A,B)@t, rewrite U(A,B)@r as the re-anchored bad*(r), re-anchor the guard-failure condition at its rightmost witness) and survives all three probe models including the one that refutes GHR's printed formula; the six probe theorems compile. Cases 6, 7 and 8 yielded no pinned candidate: their guard-failure conditions are exists-forall over the window (s,t], whose re-anchoring retains an s-bounded forward conjunct with no analogue of Case 5's collapse, so the re-anchoring does not terminate at a fixed finite formula. Primary contingency branch of the plan taken: Phase 7 and the phases downstream close as COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS; Phases 1-6 and 14-15 land.

Phases 1-4 landed first-try or near-first-try: Syntax.lean compiled on the first build, and the usTruth_swap_congr duality combinator reduced every past-side statement of GHR 10.2.1 and 10.2.2 to a single simpa line. Packaging the duality once, as the plan's Phase 3 directed, paid for itself immediately.

GHR Lemma 10.2.3 Cases 6, 7 and 8 have no candidate right-hand side. Their guard-failure condition is an exists-forall over the window below the evaluation point, and re-anchoring it at its rightmost witness retains a forward-looking bounded conjunct that cannot be an S-guard; the negation route between Cases 5 and 8 is circular. GHR 10.2.4 consumes all eight cases, so Theorem 10.2.9 and every deliverable resting on it are unreachable without them. Recorded in specs/867_formalize_gabbay_separation_ztime/prototype/cases-5-8-probe.lean's ## Gate measurement and in the plan's Phase 5 #### Reasoned Exclusions.

Phase 16: GHR vol.1 ch.10 section 10.2 markdown chunk (ch1001) carries the FULL printed text of Lemma 10.2.3's eight cases, including the generic negated-since distribution identity at Case 8 and the explicit reduction sentences for Cases 6, 7, 8. Reading it directly replaced the plan's reconstructed one-line DAG with source-quoted edges and supplied Case 7's and Case 6's own semantic steps, which the plan's summary had compressed away.

Phase 16 gate: the two-disjunct Case 5 bracketing repair the plan told Phase 17 to prefer is REFUTED by a new model (a={0}, q=empty, A={1,5}, B={2,3,4}, t=2), compiled as v3_not_twoDisjRhs beside v3_LHS. Both printed bracketings keep not-S(not-q,not-A) as a conjunct of the second disjunct, and at that point the LHS holds while both S(a,B) and not-S(not-q,not-A) fail. Phase 5's case5RHS fallback is unrefuted but has no correctness derivation on record. Pinned a third candidate instead: GHR's own Core with W moved from a shared conjunct to a case split, with a full semantic derivation (Claim C) in the prototype.

Phases 18 and 19 both land in ElimHard.lean and were committed together rather than one commit per phase. Phase 18 was build-verified green on its own (scoped guarded build, exit 0) before Phase 19 began, but no commit was fired at that boundary, so the two cannot now be separated without rewriting the file. Deviation from the phase-checkpoint protocol's one-commit-per-phase rule.

All eight cases of GHR Lemma 10.2.3 now compile sorry-free. Phase 5 had declared Cases 6, 7 and 8 unreachable with a precisely-located obstruction; the obstruction was entirely an artefact of the direct semantic re-anchoring route. Reading the source's own reduction sentences gave each case in under one module: Case 8 from the generic negated-since identity plus Case 5 twice and Case 2 at q := top, Case 7 from one semantic step plus Cases 4 and 8, Case 6 from one first-not-B-point step plus Cases 3 and 5.

Phase 20: general dnf/cnf on the Boolean skeleton were not built. The untl-literal normal form (substU plus the event and guard splits) was built instead: it isolates plus-or-minus untl B A, the only literal 10.2.4 consumes, and yields exactly the four hard-case constituents with no leftover clause shapes. GHR 10.2.1's two distributivities and the clause-by-clause case application are unchanged. Recorded in the plan's Phase 20 Reasoned Exclusions and in NormalForm.lean's docstring.

NEW precisely-located obstruction at GHR 10.2.4's second conclusion clause (untl occurs only as untl B A). The landed case2Rhs of Eliminations.lean composes case1Rhs at transformed parameters plus allFuture, introducing the untl types untl A.neg (A.neg.and B.neg) and untl top A.neg.neg; GHR's printed Case 2 avoids both by folding G-not-A or U(not-A and not-B, not-A) back to not-U(A,B) via 10.2.2 in reverse, which the landed proof omits. case3Rhs inherits it, and case6Rhs/case7Rhs/case8Rhs inherit it in turn, so three of sepSnce's four constituents carry extra untl types. Blocks Phase 21's uTypeCount induction as the plan specifies it. Additive repair, no signature change: a second Case 2 lemma at GHR's printed three-disjunct RHS.

Phase 21 is BLOCKED on a NEW obstruction, different from the one Phase 5 recorded. uTypeCount -- the plan's measure, the number of distinct maximal untl subformulas -- cannot carry GHR 10.2.6's induction over the eliminations as landed, because Phase 20's sepSnce can increase it. Cause: Eliminations.lean's landed case2Rhs is built as (... ) or case1Rhs a q (A.neg.and B.neg) A.neg together with allFuture A.neg, so it carries the untl types untl A.neg (A.neg.and B.neg) and untl top A.neg.neg beside untl B A; GHR's printed Case 2 carries neither, because its third step folds G-not-A or U(not-A and not-B, not-A) back into not-U(A,B) by Lemma 10.2.2 in reverse, which the landed proof omits. case3Rhs consumes case2Rhs, and case6Rhs/case7Rhs/case8Rhs consume case3Rhs/case8Rhs, so three of sepSnce's four constituents inherit it. Two repair routes, both recorded in the plan's Phase 21 blocker entry: (1) add a second Case 2 lemma at GHR's printed three-disjunct right-hand side and re-derive Cases 3, 6, 7, 8 through it -- additive, no signature change, and uTypeCount then works as specified; (2) change the measure to count untl occurrences under a snce rather than distinct untl types -- leaves the landed layer untouched but redesigns the measures of Phases 21, 22 and 23. Choosing between them is a planning decision, not an implementation one.; Phases 22-27 are NOT STARTED, gated behind Phase 21. The plan's own standing warning is unchanged: Phase 23's junction-depth strict decrease is asserted without proof in the source and is the plan's primary stall candidate; it has still never been reached.
